The quarter unfolded, as these things tend to, in relative quiet. The Simulated Wire logged a session or two of genuine somnolence, and the data prints that mattered — CPI at 2.9%, policy rate holding at 5.00% — came in exactly where the consensus expected them to land. There is a temptation, in moments like this, to overread stillness as signal. We resist that temptation. Markets that stop shouting are not necessarily markets that have stopped moving; they are markets catching their breath before the next repricing. High yield spreads at 400bps tell a story of credit markets that remain cautious but orderly — not seized, not euphoric, simply pricing risk with more discipline than they did at the top of the cycle we entered our flagship into.

That discipline matters to us directly. Our 2021-vintage flagship was built in an era of full prices and full leverage, and the carrying cost of that leverage has been the dominant feature of recent quarters. This quarter, however, brought a measure of stability rather than further erosion. NAV index sits at 101.1, and the fund posted a reported return of +1.1% for the quarter, matching year-to-date at +1.1% and extending since-inception performance to +33.0%. Public equities returned +1.3% over the same period — a narrow gap, and one we'd characterize as noise rather than signal.
